slides.title: Doors only staff may open
slides.text: At the post office, some doors only staff may open. That rule decides who can get to the letters inside, and who must stay out.

slides.title: Your tablet does it too
slides.text: A tablet lock screen does the same job at home. Only a person with permission, and the right key or code, can open it and see inside.
slides.alt: A tablet holds messages and pictures. Signing out on a shared computer: does the habit protect it, or is it risky?

focus.cue: A tablet holds your messages and pictures: sort what protects it
Protects it, or risky? You decide for each habit

slides.title: A found key is not enough
slides.text: Mina loses her mailbox key, and a stranger finds it. A second lock still keeps her mailbox shut, because the stranger is missing one more thing.
steps: a second lock asks for a code
a code arrives on a phone at home
slides.alt: A trouble card: a guesser tries key after key on a mailbox. The layer tiles: Padlock Gate, Key Checker, Patch Crew, Copy Vault.

focus.cue: A guesser tries key after key on a mailbox
A second lock, the key checker, still stands

slides.title: A spare copy, kept elsewhere
slides.text: A backup is a spare copy of your things, kept somewhere else, like photos saved in another place. A backup is for your things, never for your secrets.
slides.alt: A Good Spare Copy: the sorting round that tells a real backup, kept somewhere else, from a copy that is not.

focus.cue: A copy in the family's online folder: a spare kept elsewhere
A good spare copy, or not a spare copy?

slides.title: The wrong person
slides.text: Finding a tablet on a bench does not make it yours to open. A letter that asks for your mailbox key is the wrong person too: only you and a trusted adult may know it.
slides.alt: A letter from Post Office Team, “Your mailbox will close”, with clues marked: your mailbox key, and today.

focus.cue: Anyone can type "Post Office Team" on a letter
It asks for your mailbox key: no permission

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Trick Inbox at Prize Letters and sort all 6 letters. Tap every clue, then choose a move. Some letters ask for your mailbox key, but only you and a trusted adult may know it.
slides.alt: A letter, “You won a tablet!”, with clues marked: you are our lucky winner; your mailbox key; in the next ten minutes.
